translation_en: Musa ibn Ismail narrated to us; Abd al-Wahid narrated to us; Asim narrated to us, who said: I asked Anas, “Did the Messenger of Allah declare Madinah a sanctuary?” He said, “Yes, from this place to that place; its trees must not be cut. Whoever introduces an offense in it will incur the curse of Allah, the angels, and all people.” Asim said: Musa ibn Anas informed me that Anas also said, “or whoever gives shelter to an offender.”

Said ibn Talid narrated to us; Ibn Wahb narrated to me; Abd al-Rahman ibn Shurayh and another narrated to me, from Abu al-Aswad, from Urwah, who said: Abdullah ibn Amr came to us as a pilgrim, and I heard him say: I heard the Prophet say: “Allah does not take knowledge away from people after giving it to them by snatching it away. Rather, He takes knowledge away by taking the scholars along with their knowledge. Then ignorant people remain, who are asked for rulings and give their opinions, so they go astray and lead others astray.” I told Aishah, the wife of the Prophet, about this. Later Abdullah ibn Amr came on pilgrimage again, and she said, “Nephew, go to Abdullah and confirm for me what you told me he had said.” I went to him and asked him, and he told it to me in much the same way. I went to Aishah and informed her, and she was amazed and said, “By Allah, Abdullah ibn Amr remembered it correctly.”

Abdan informed us; Abu Hamzah informed us. I heard al-Amash say: I asked Abu Wa’il, “Were you present at Siffin?” He said, “Yes.” I heard Sahl ibn Hunayf say: “People, be wary of your own opinions when it comes to your religion. I saw myself on the day of Abu Jandal. If I had been able to reject the Messenger of Allah’s decision, I would have rejected it. Whenever we placed our swords on our shoulders in response to something that horrified us, it led us toward something we recognized as easier than this matter.” Abu Wa’il said: I witnessed Siffin, and what a terrible battle Siffin was.

Ali ibn Abdullah narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us, who said: I heard Ibn al-Munkadir say: I heard Jabir ibn Abdullah say: I fell ill, and the Messenger of Allah came to visit me, with Abu Bakr, and they were walking. They came to me while I had lost consciousness. The Messenger of Allah performed ablution, then poured some of his ablution water over me, and I regained consciousness. I said, “Messenger of Allah”—or, Sufyan said, “I said, ‘O Messenger of Allah’”—“how should I dispose of my property? What should I do with my property?” He did not answer me until the verse concerning inheritance was revealed.

Musaddad narrated to us; Abu Awanah narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Asbahani, from Abu Salih Dhakwan, from Abu Said: A woman came to the Messenger of Allah and said, “Messenger of Allah, the men have taken all your teaching. Set aside a day for us when we can come to you and you can teach us what Allah has taught you.” He said: “Gather on such-and-such a day at such-and-such a place.” They gathered, and the Messenger of Allah came to them and taught them some of what Allah had taught him. Then he said: “Any woman among you who has sent three of her children ahead of her will have them as a shield from the Fire.” One woman asked, “And two, Messenger of Allah?” He repeated it twice, then said: “And two, and two, and two.”

Ubaydullah ibn Musa narrated to us, from Ismail, from Qays, from al-Mughirah ibn Shubah, from the Prophet, who said: “A group from my community will continue to prevail until Allah’s command comes to them while they are prevailing.”

Ismail narrated to us; Ibn Wahb narrated to us, from Yunus, from Ibn Shihab. Humayd informed me; I heard Muawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan preaching, and he said: I heard the Prophet say: “For whomever Allah intends good, He grants understanding of the religion. I only distribute, while Allah gives. The affairs of this community will continue to remain upright until the Hour is established—or until Allah’s command comes.”

Ali ibn Abdullah narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us. Amr said: I heard Jabir ibn Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with them both, say: When this was revealed to the Messenger of Allah—“Say: He is the One Able to send punishment upon you from above you” (6:65)—he said, “I seek refuge in Your Face.” And when this was revealed—“or from beneath your feet”—he said, “I seek refuge in Your Face.” When this was revealed—“or to confuse you in sects and make some of you taste the violence of others”—he said: “These two are easier—or less severe.”

Asbagh ibn al-Faraj narrated to us; Ibn Wahb narrated to me, from Yunus, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah: A Bedouin came to the Messenger of Allah and said, “My wife gave birth to a dark-skinned boy, and I disown him.” The Messenger of Allah said: “Do you have camels?” He said, “Yes.” He asked, “What colors are they?” He said, “Red.” He asked, “Are any of them gray?” He replied, “There are indeed some gray ones among them.” He asked, “How do you think that came about?” He said, “Messenger of Allah, it is an inherited trait.” The Prophet said: “Perhaps this child has inherited a trait.” He did not allow the man to disown him.

Musaddad narrated to us; Abu Awanah narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Said ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: A woman came to the Prophet and said, “My mother vowed to perform pilgrimage, but she died before doing so. May I perform it on her behalf?” He said: “Yes, perform pilgrimage on her behalf. What do you think? If your mother owed a debt, would you pay it?” She said, “Yes.” He said: “Then pay what is owed to Allah, for Allah has the greatest right that a vow be fulfilled.”

Shihab ibn Abbad narrated to us; Ibrahim ibn Humayd narrated to us, from Ismail, from Qays, from Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: “There is no envy except in two cases: a man whom Allah has given wealth and enabled to spend it in what is right, and another whom Allah has given wisdom, so he judges by it and teaches it.”

Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us; Ibn Abi Dhib narrated to us, from al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet, who said: “The Hour will not come until my community follows the ways of the generations before it, inch by inch and cubit by cubit.” It was said, “Like Persia and Rome?” He said: “Who else among the people?”

Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz narrated to us; Abu Umar al-Sanani, from Yemen, narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ata ibn Yasar, from Abu Said al-Khudri, from the Prophet, who said: “You will surely follow the ways of those who came before you, inch by inch and cubit by cubit, until if they entered a lizard’s hole, you would follow them.” We said, “Messenger of Allah, the Jews and Christians?” He said, “Who else?”

Al-Humaydi narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us; al-Amash narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Murrah, from Masruq, from Abdullah, who said: The Prophet said: “No person is killed unjustly without the first son of Adam bearing a share of its guilt”—Sufyan may have said, “of its blood”—“because he was the first to set the practice of killing.”

Ismail narrated to me; Malik narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Salami: A Bedouin pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah upon Islam. Fever struck him in Madinah, and he came to the Messenger of Allah and said, “Messenger of Allah, release me from my pledge.” The Messenger of Allah refused. He came again and said, “Release me from my pledge,” and the Prophet refused. He came a third time and asked to be released, and the Prophet refused. The Bedouin then left. The Messenger of Allah said: “Madinah is like a furnace: it removes its impurities and its good becomes pure.”

Musa ibn Ismail narrated to us; Abd al-Wahid narrated to us; Mamar narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah, who said: Ibn Abbas told me: I used to teach Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf. During the last pilgrimage Umar performed, Abd al-Rahman said at Mina, “If you had seen the Commander of the Faithful when a man came to him and said, ‘So-and-so says that if the Commander of the Faithful dies, we will pledge allegiance to so-and-so.’” Umar said, “This evening I will stand and warn these men who want to seize authority from them.” I said, “Do not do that. The pilgrimage season gathers all sorts of people, who will overwhelm your gathering. I fear they will not understand your words properly, and every busybody will carry them away and spread them. Wait until you reach Madinah, the home of emigration and the Sunnah, where you can speak privately with the Companions of the Messenger of Allah among the Emigrants and Ansar. They will preserve what you say and understand it as you intended.” He said, “By Allah, I will make this speech at the first opportunity I have in Madinah.” Ibn Abbas said: We arrived in Madinah, and Umar said: “Allah sent Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, with the truth and revealed the Book to him. Among what was revealed was the verse of stoning...”

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us; Hammad narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Muhammad, who said: We were with Abu Hurayrah, who was wearing two linen garments dyed with safflower. He blew his nose and said, “Well, well! Abu Hurayrah blows his nose in linen! I remember when I used to fall unconscious between the pulpit of the Messenger of Allah and Aishah’s chamber. Someone would come and put his foot on my neck, thinking I was insane. I was not insane; I was only hungry.”

Muhammad ibn Kathir informed us; Sufyan informed us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abis, who said: Ibn Abbas was asked, “Did you attend the Eid prayer with the Prophet?” He said, “Yes. If I had not held a special position with him, I would not have attended because I was so young.” He went to the marker by the house of Kathir ibn al-Salt, prayed, and then gave a sermon. He did not mention a call to prayer or a call to begin it. Then he ordered charity, and the women began pointing to their ears and throats. He ordered Bilal to go to them, and then Bilal returned to the Prophet.
Abu Nuaym narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Dinar, from Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both: The Prophet used to come to Quba on foot and riding.

Ayyub ibn Sulayman narrated to us; Abu Bakr ibn Abi Uways narrated to us, from Sulayman ibn Bilal, from Salih ibn Kaysan. Ibn Shihab said: Anas ibn Malik informed me that the Messenger of Allah used to pray the afternoon prayer, then go to the highlands while the sun was still high. Al-Layth added, from Yunus: The highlands were four or three miles away.

Amr ibn Zurarah narrated to us; al-Qasim ibn Malik narrated to us, from al-Juayd. I heard al-Saib ibn Yazid say: In the time of the Prophet, the Sa was one and one-third of your current mudd. It was later increased. Al-Qasim ibn Malik heard this from al-Juayd.

Abdullah ibn Maslamah narrated to us, from Malik, from Ishaq ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah, from Anas ibn Malik: The Messenger of Allah said: “O Allah, bless their measures for them, and bless their Sa and their mudd for them”—meaning the people of Madinah.

Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir narrated to us; Abu Damrah narrated to us; Musa ibn Uqbah narrated to us, from Nafi, from Ibn Umar: The Jews brought a man and a woman who had committed adultery to the Prophet. He ordered that they be stoned, and they were stoned near the place where funeral biers were set beside the mosque.

Ismail narrated to me; Malik narrated to me, from Amr, the freedman of al-Muttalib, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him: Mount Uhud appeared before the Messenger of Allah, and he said: “This is a mountain that loves us and we love it. O Allah, Ibrahim declared Mecca sacred, and I declare sacred what lies between the two lava fields.” Sahl also reported from the Prophet regarding Uhud.

Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us; Abu Ghassan narrated to us; Abu Hazim narrated to me, from Sahl, who said: Between the mosque wall on the qiblah side and the pulpit there was space for a sheep to pass.

Amr ibn Ali narrated to us; Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us; Malik narrated to us, from Khubayb ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Hafs ibn Asim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: “Between my house and my pulpit is a garden from the gardens of Paradise, and my pulpit is above my pool.”

Musa ibn Ismail narrated to us; Juwayriyah narrated to us, from Nafi, from Abdullah, who said: The Prophet held a race between horses. The trained horses ran from al-Hafya to Thaniyyat al-Wada, and the untrained horses ran from Thaniyyat al-Wada to the mosque of Banu Zurayq. Abdullah was among those who raced. Qutaybah narrated to us, from Layth, from Nafi, from Ibn Umar.

Qutaybah narrated to us, from Layth, from Nafi, from Ibn Umar. (Another chain:) Ishaq narrated to me; Isa, Ibn Idris, and Ibn Abi Ghaniyyah informed us, from Abu Hayyan, from al-Shabi, from Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: I heard Umar while he was on the Prophet’s pulpit.
Abu al-Yaman informed us; Shuaib informed us, from al-Zuhri. Al-Saib ibn Yazid informed me that he heard Uthman ibn Affan preach to us from the Prophet’s pulpit.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us; Abd al-Ala narrated to us; Hisham ibn Hassan narrated to us, that Hisham ibn Urwah narrated to him, from his father, that Aishah said: This basin would be placed for me and the Messenger of Allah, and we would both draw water from it together.
